note_text: Binary search finds a target in a sorted array by repeatedly checking the middle element and halving the search range.
A model card documents intended use, limitations, evaluation, and known risks of a machine-learning system.
Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are correct; recall is the fraction of actual positives found.
A variable stores a value in memory. Python uses assignment with the equals sign, and variable names should be meaningful.
A Git commit records a snapshot of project changes. Branches let developers work on features separately.
A short note: recursion calls the same function again until a base case stops it.
A database table contains rows and columns. A primary key uniquely identifies each record.
Multi-factor authentication combines independent evidence such as a password and a one-time code.
A database JOIN combines related rows from two tables using a matching column.
The model achieved high precision but low recall, so many relevant positive examples were missed.
A hash table maps keys to values and typically supports average constant-time lookup.
A software requirement states a user need or system behavior and should be testable and unambiguous.
Merge sort divides an array, sorts each half recursively, and merges the sorted halves in O(n log n) time.
A bar chart compares categories, while a line chart is useful for showing change over time.
A stack follows last-in first-out order. Push adds an item and pop removes the most recent item.
Probability ranges from zero to one and quantifies how likely an event is.
A dashboard uses charts and summary metrics to communicate patterns in a dataset.
Cross-validation repeats training and validation across folds to estimate how a model generalizes.
